name: Claude (Anthropic)
enables: Use Claude models through your own Anthropic API account, billed by Anthropic.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live run pending.

name: OpenAI
enables: Use OpenAI models for coding and analysis with your own API key.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live run pending.

name: Google Gemini
enables: Use Gemini models through your own Google API key. This is the Gemini API, separate from Gemini CLI.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live run pending.

name: OpenAI-compatible endpoints
enables: Connect any service or gateway that speaks the OpenAI chat API by entering its address and key.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: OpenRouter
enables: A first-class gateway to many models with one account, with approved models, providers, privacy and budget policies. Billed by OpenRouter, never from a coding CLI subscription.
note: Tested against recorded responses; live run pending.

name: BytePlus ModelArk
enables: Use ModelArk models directly, where the service's terms allow it.

name: Ollama
enables: Detect Ollama, pull and remove models, and route suitable work to models on your own hardware.
note: No live model run recorded yet.

name: LM Studio
enables: Use the models you have loaded in LM Studio, entirely on your machine.
note: No live model run recorded yet.

name: llama.cpp-compatible servers
enables: Use a local model server you run yourself.
note: Through its OpenAI-compatible server.

name: Claude Code
enables: Use the Claude Code you are already signed in to on your machine as a Factory worker. Vekrun detects its version and sign-in and never copies your login anywhere.
note: Run end to end with a real session. Its work moves into isolated environments through the Vekrun bridge as that ships.

name: Codex
enables: Use your signed-in Codex CLI on your machine as a Factory worker. Vekrun detects its version and sign-in.
note: Tested against a stand-in; no live run yet.

name: Gemini CLI
enables: Use your signed-in Gemini CLI on your machine as a Factory worker.

name: GitHub CLI
enables: Discover, install and update the GitHub CLI on your Host and use it for repository and pull request work.

name: SSH remotes
enables: Open a shell on a remote machine in a Vekrun tab, with the host's key checked before you connect.

name: Remote workers
enables: Run agent tasks on a workstation or server you control, so they keep going after you close your laptop.
note: A headless worker runs unattended, and a remote Vekrun is reached over an SSH tunnel with reconnect. Verified on macOS only.

name: Language servers
enables: Diagnostics and navigation in the code view when you inspect or take over a job.

name: Custom MCP servers
enables: Give agents access to any MCP server you configure, with permissions you set per server.
note: Remote and local servers with per-server permissions; every call asks.

name: Linear
enables: Turn assigned issues into coding sessions and send status back when you deliver.
note: Start Work and the agent and Factory handoff work on every Board ticket. The connection is tested against recorded responses; live sync and status updates are not yet verified.

name: Jira
enables: Work on tickets and update their progress without leaving the terminal.
note: Start Work and the agent and Factory handoff work on every Board ticket. The connection is tested against recorded responses; live sync and status updates are not yet verified.

name: Asana
enables: See your Asana tasks on the Board and start work from any of them.
note: Start Work and the agent and Factory handoff work on every Board ticket. The connection is tested against recorded responses; live sync and status updates are not yet verified.

name: GitHub Issues
enables: See assigned GitHub issues, open them in Vekrun, and start work manually, with an AI agent, or with Factory.
note: Start Work and the agent and Factory handoff work on every Board ticket. The GitHub connection is tested against recorded responses; live sync and status updates are not yet verified.

name: GitLab Issues
enables: Bring GitLab issues into your development workspace and turn them into coding tasks.
note: Start Work and the agent and Factory handoff work on every Board ticket. The GitLab connection and sign-in are tested against recorded responses; live sync is not yet verified.

name: Confluence
enables: Let agents read the specs and pages behind your tickets.
note: Shares one connection with Jira.

name: Notion
enables: Let agents read and update the Notion pages your work refers to.

name: Git
enables: Stage, diff, commit, branch, stash and manage worktrees using the git you already have installed, so your hooks keep working.

name: GitHub
enables: Repositories, pull requests, reviews and checks. Pull requests open with the plan and evidence attached.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: GitLab
enables: Review merge requests, manage code, and link changes to issues.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: Honeybadger
enables: Investigate application errors and turn incidents into development work.
note: Errors, occurrences and projects are read through the Data API and tested against recorded responses; not yet run against a live account.

name: Sentry
enables: Analyze errors and performance problems, then plan or delegate fixes.
note: Issues, events and performance problems are read through the API and tested against recorded responses; not yet run against a live organisation.

name: Datadog
enables: Examine traces, latency, and application health to identify bottlenecks.
note: Error tracking, monitors and slowest endpoints by p95 are read through the API and tested against recorded responses; trace search is not claimed until verified live.

name: AppSignal
enables: Investigate exceptions, slow requests, and performance regressions.
note: Apps, exception and performance incidents and samples are read through the API and tested against recorded responses; not yet run against a live account.

name: PagerDuty
enables: Turn an active incident into an investigation, engineering tickets and a verified fix. Acknowledging or closing stays yours.

name: incident.io
enables: Bring incident timelines and affected services into an investigation and draft the follow-up work.

name: GitHub Actions
enables: Open a failed run, see which job and test broke, and work on a repair directly in Vekrun.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: GitLab CI/CD
enables: Investigate failed pipelines and jobs and link the fix to the merge request.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: Docker and Compose
enables: Docker Compose projects are discovered and started for a job, alone or alongside native services.
note: Runs real projects on the host today; isolated environments are next.

name: Playwright, Vitest, Jest, pytest, RSpec, Cypress
enables: Framework-aware test runs with parsed results, failure summaries and test-to-source mapping as verification evidence.
note: Uses the project’s own test runner.

name: Slack
enables: Let agents read the threads behind a task and post updates where your team works.
note: A ready-made preset with sign-in exists; not yet run against the live service.

name: Figma
enables: Let agents read the designs a ticket refers to.
note: Preset ships once Figma lists Vekrun.

name: PostgreSQL
enables: Let agents inspect a database schema and run read queries you approve.
note: No vendor-hosted server; a local server you run.

name: Cloudflare Workers and Pages
enables: See deployments, link them to commits, inspect failures, and verify repairs against production monitoring.
note: Reading Cloudflare through its MCP preset exists; the deployment workflow is planned.

name: Vercel
enables: See deployments and their status, link them to the change that caused them, and inspect failures.

name: Railway
enables: Follow a deployment from commit to running service and check production afterwards.

name: Render
enables: Link releases to code changes and inspect failed deploys where you code.

name: Fly.io
enables: See releases and machine status and tie a deploy to the production signals that follow.

name: GitHub Code Scanning and CodeQL
enables: Turn a scanner finding into an investigation, a prepared fix and a reviewable pull request.
note: Tested against recorded responses.

name: Semgrep
enables: Bring Semgrep findings with their exact code locations into repair planning and verification.

name: SonarQube
enables: Investigate quality and security findings from SonarQube Cloud or Server and prepare verified fixes.

name: Snyk
enables: Act on dependency and code vulnerabilities with a repair plan, not an automatic change.

name: LaunchDarkly
enables: Correlate a rollout with the errors or latency that followed it. Vekrun never changes a flag for you.

name: PostHog
enables: Bring product analytics and flag context into an investigation of a regression.

name: GrowthBook
enables: See which experiment or flag was live when a problem started.

name: Statsig
enables: Rollout context for regression investigations.

name: Supabase
enables: Inspect and manage Supabase projects from a session, with your permission.
note: A ready-made preset with sign-in exists; not yet run against the live service.

name: Stripe
enables: Look up Stripe objects while debugging payment code, with your permission.
note: A ready-made preset with sign-in exists; not yet run against the live service.

name: Grafana Cloud
enables: Dashboards and alerts as investigation context.

name: New Relic
enables: Errors and traces through the same Insights workspace.

name: Elastic and Kibana
enables: Log search and APM data for investigations.

name: OpenSearch
enables: Log search for investigations.

name: Bugsnag
enables: Error groups and stability data in Insights.

name: Rollbar
enables: Error items and occurrences in Insights.

name: Neon
enables: Schema and read-only queries while investigating.

name: PlanetScale
enables: Schema and read-only queries while investigating.

name: Redis
enables: Inspect keys and stats, read-only by default.

name: MongoDB Atlas
enables: Schema and read-only queries while investigating.

name: AWS RDS
enables: Database context, read-only by default.

name: Firebase
enables: Backend context for investigations.

name: Microsoft Teams
enables: Read the threads behind a task and post updates with your permission.

name: Google Drive
enables: Pull requirements and documents into a plan.

name: Postman and OpenAPI
enables: Understand an API from its specification while planning or investigating.
